children: By Mariapaula Gonzalez
The reports were true: Royal Caribbean Group is buying a 50% ownership stake in Sandals Resorts.
Royal Caribbean will be acquiring a 50% stake in Sandals Resorts for roughly $3 billion-the largest deal in the cruise giant's history. The transaction is expected to close early next year.
Investors weren't exactly pleased Tuesday when the Financial Times reported speculation of a deal valuing Sandals at over $6 billion. Royal Caribbean shares fell 6.1% after the report.
The transaction was confirmed in a press release Wednesday by both companies. Royal Caribbean stock rose 0.5% in premarket trading to $235.50.
After reports surfaced Tuesday afternoon, analysts at Stifel had one question on their minds: "What the heck are they thinking?"

They wrote Tuesday that investor skepticism driving the stock down may have stemmed from a demographic mismatch: While Sandals operates resorts for adults and couples, Royal Caribbean's core brand targets family vacations.
Stifel analysts also noted investor fears that cruise growth in the Caribbean may be reaching a limit. They questioned whether softening cruise demand in 2027 and beyond prompted a risky pivot.
But all hope isn't yet lost.

"If this wasn't RCL's management team, we would be running for the hills if this deal ultimately came together," the analysts wrote. "At this point, we think you have to give them the benefit of the doubt before jumping to the conclusion that a deal like this wouldn't eventually be massively accretive."

Stifel estimated that Royal Caribbean could shut a couple of the Sandals resorts down and build new private island concepts throughout the Caribbean, which could boost yields. The firm maintained a Buy rating on the stock and a $415 price target.
The new venture will expand Royal Caribbean's business beyond cruise ships into "land-based" vacations, allowing them to offer land-and-sea vacation packages to their customers.

Jefferies analysts chimed in after the deal's announcement, expressing a bullish stance. The firm said the lines between cruises and land resorts are converging and that adding land-based resorts is the natural next step for Royal Caribbean as it works to capture a larger portion of the $2 trillion global vacation market. Jefferies has a Hold rating on the stock with a $305 price target.

Royal Caribbean's purchase is expected to generate $300 million in annual earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. When reports broke Tuesday, the market's negative reaction wiped out $4 billion in equity value, according to Mizuho analyst Ben Chaiken.

The analyst added that the market's negative reaction "doesn't add up" and that wiping out $4 billion in equity value was unjustified since the deal is expected to be profitable. He maintained an Outperform rating on the stock with a $380 price target.
As part of the deal, Sandals will get a large influx of capital and funding through Royal Caribbean and debt financing from Morgan Stanley, according to the press release.
Both chief executives, Royal Caribbean's Jason Liberty and Sandals' Adam Stewart, will lead the new board together. Sandals will maintain its brand identity and operational leadership.
Existing bookings, loyalty programs, and resort or cruise operations will continue as usual. After the deal closes, travels can likely expect cross-promotions and bundled cruise and resort vacations.
